title: Facilitating Humanitarian Aid and Fundraising Efforts following Ceasefire in Israel and Hamas Conflict
what_it_is: Facilitating Humanitarian Aid and Fundraising Efforts following Ceasefire in Israel and Hamas Conflict

sections.label: Singapore welcomes ceasefire agreement
sections.summary: Singapore welcomes the multi-phase ceasefire and hostage release agreement announced on 15 January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: First, Singapore welcomes the multi-phase ceasefire and hostage release agreement that was announced on 15 January 2025.

sections.label: Singapore humanitarian aid to Gaza
sections.summary: Singapore has sent six tranches of aid to Gaza worth over S$19 million and plans a seventh.

sentences.text: Since the start of the Israel-Hamas conflict in October 2023, Singapore and Singaporeans have contributed significantly.
We have, so far, conveyed six tranches of humanitarian assistance to Gaza.
These six tranches account for more than S$19 million.

In fact, Minister Maliki Osman just visited Jordan two weeks ago to witness the handover of the sixth tranche, which comprising almost S$1.3 million that were raised by the Rahmatan Lil Alamin Foundation (RLAF), and this was given to the Jordan Hashemite Charity Organisation and to the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF).
We are making plans for a seventh tranche of humanitarian aid and this will consist of food, essential supplies and medical supplies.

sections.label: Singapore backs two-state solution
sections.summary: Singapore supports a Palestinian homeland and a negotiated two-state solution consistent with UN Security Council resolutions.

sentences.text: Singapore supports the right of the Palestinian people to a homeland of their own.

We believe that the only viable path for achieving a comprehensive, just and durable solution to this long-standing conflict is a negotiated two-state solution, consistent with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions.

sections.label: Scholarships and training for Palestinians
sections.summary: Singapore is expanding undergraduate and postgraduate scholarships for Palestinian scholars and training Palestinian Authority bureaucrats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And that means, especially on education, on scholarships.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We are, in fact, expanding our scholarships to both at the undergraduate and postgraduate levels to deserving Palestinian scholars who will get in on their merit.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will also work closely to provide training opportunities for the bureaucrats in the Palestinian Authority, because they need to step up capacity if they are able to engage not only in reconstruction but ultimately, in administering a state of their own in a constructive way.

sections.label: Aid accounting and effectiveness
sections.summary: Through RLAF, S$19 million in aid has gone to Gaza, with Singaporeans concerned about its effectiveness and accounting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As of January this year, through RLAF, we have provided S$19 million in terms of aid to the people of Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What is also important in the minds of Singaporeans who have contributed most generously to this effort, is the assessment of the effectiveness of the aid provided and whether it has been properly accounted for?

sections.label: Donations to Jordan and UNICEF
sections.summary: Almost $1.3 million was donated to the Jordan Hashemite Charity Organisation and UNICEF, focusing on children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Almost $1.3 million dollars were donated to the Jordan Hashemite Charity Organisation and to UNICEF focusing especially and obviously, on children.

sections.label: Multi-phase ceasefire in place
sections.summary: A multi-phase ceasefire is what is in place now.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: What we have in place now is a multi-phase ceasefire.

sections.label: Phase two and three complicated
sections.summary: Phase two and phase three are going to be very, very complicated.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Having said all that, phase two and phase three are going to be very, very complicated.

sections.label: Israelis and Palestinians know position
sections.summary: Israelis and Palestinians engaged know the position that Palestinians need their own state.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Both the Israelis and the Palestinians whom we have engaged know our position.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We believe the Palestinians need their own state.

sections.label: Dire needs and sustainable peace
sections.summary: Dire needs and infrastructural needs exist, but sustainable peace remains the key impediment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Mr Tan is right, there are dire needs on the ground and there are dire infrastructural needs – housing, utilities, water, electricity, hospitals, schools.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But, actually, the key impediment to all this still remains a sustainable peace.
